message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Lint files
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck files
        run: npm run typecheck

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          lfs: true

      - name: Setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Setup ccache
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-ccache
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          key: tests-${{ hashFiles('vendor/VERSIONS') }}
          max-size: 300M

      - name: Run ts unit tests
        run: npm test -- --maxWorkers=2 --coverage

      - name: Run c++ unit tests
        run: |
          cd tests
          chmod +x build_and_test.sh run_tests.sh
          ./build_and_test.sh
          ./run_tests.sh

      - name: Save ccache
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/save-ccache

  build-ios-from-source:
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          bootstrap: metal

      # React Native itself is most of this build and only changes with the
      # example's dependencies, so this cache is not tied to the llama.cpp version.
      - name: Setup ccache
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-ccache
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          key: ios-from-source
          max-size: 1500M

      - name: Cache build & pods
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          path: |
            example/ios/Pods
            example/ios/build
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pods-${{ hashFiles('example/ios/Podfile.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pods-

      - name: Upgrade CocoaPods to version 1.15.2
        run: |
          gem uninstall cocoapods --ignore-dependencies
          gem install cocoapods -v 1.15.2

      - name: Install cocoapods
        run: |
          npm run example run pods

      - name: Build example for iOS
        run: |
          npm run build:ios

      - name: Save ccache
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/save-ccache

  # Every xcframework slice compiles the whole library, so the slices are split
  # over parallel jobs: this one and build-ios-framework-slices. This job builds
  # the slice the example app runs on and proves the prebuilt path with it.
  # (All slices are packaged together by the release and sync workflows.)
  build-ios-frameworks:
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          bootstrap: metal

      - name: Setup ccache
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-ccache
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          key: ios-frameworks-simulator
          max-size: 1500M

      - name: Cache build & pods
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          path: |
            example/ios/Pods
            example/ios/build
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pods-${{ hashFiles('example/ios/Podfile.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pods-

      - name: Upgrade CocoaPods to version 1.15.2
        run: |
          gem uninstall cocoapods --ignore-dependencies
          gem install cocoapods -v 1.15.2

      - name: Install cocoapods
        run: |
          npm run example run pods
        env:
          RNLLAMA_BUILD_FROM_SOURCE: 0

      - name: Build frameworks
        run: |
          ./scripts/build-ios.sh ios-simulator

      - name: Build example for iOS
        run: |
          npm run build:ios

      - name: Save ccache
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/save-ccache

  build-ios-framework-slices:
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          # Grouped so that each job compiles for two architectures.
          - name: tvos-simulator
            slices: tvos-simulator
          - name: devices
            slices: ios-device tvos-device
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Generate embedded Metal kernels
        run: ./scripts/bootstrap.sh metal

      - name: Setup ccache
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-ccache
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          key: ios-frameworks-${{ matrix.name }}-${{ hashFiles('vendor/VERSIONS') }}
          max-size: 600M

      - name: Build frameworks
        run: |
          ./scripts/build-ios.sh ${{ matrix.slices }}

      - name: Save ccache
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/save-ccache

  build-android-from-source:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      # Runners currently have ~90 GB free, several times what this job needs.
      # Only spend time on cleaning up if that stops being true.
      - name: Free disk space if short
        run: |
          df -h /
          available_gb=$(df --output=avail -BG / | tail -n 1 | tr -dc '0-9')
          if [ "$available_gb" -lt 40 ]; then
            sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc /opt/hostedtoolcache
            df -h /
          fi

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          bootstrap: hexagon-sdk

      # Pin the JDK: with the runner's newer default, a JVM restricted-method
      # warning fails the Android Gradle Plugin's CMake configure.
      - name: Setup JDK 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 17

      - name: Cache Hexagon HTP & OpenCL artifacts
        id: htp-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          path: |
            bin
            vendor/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/v73
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-htp-${{ hashFiles('scripts/build-hexagon-htp.sh', 'scripts/build-opencl.sh', 'scripts/docker-build-wrapper.sh', 'vendor/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/**', 'vendor/OpenCL-Headers/**', 'vendor/OpenCL-ICD-Loader/**') }}

      - name: Setup ccache
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-ccache
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          key: android-src-${{ hashFiles('vendor/VERSIONS') }}
          # Debug objects carry DWARF, so they need more room than the release job's.
          max-size: 1500M

      - name: Build example for Android
        env:
          HEXAGON_SDK_VERSION: 6.7.0.0
          HEXAGON_TOOLS_VERSION: 21.0.04
          # Build only the variants that exercise distinct code paths: generic
          # CPU, arm64 with dotprod+i8mm+hexagon+opencl, and x86_64. The
          # remaining arm64 variants differ only in the -march of the ggml-cpu
          # backend; build-android-libs still builds all of them.
          ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_rnllamaVariants: rnllama,rnllama_v8_2_dotprod_i8mm_hexagon_opencl,rnllama_x86_64
          ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_rnllamaHtpArtifactsUpToDate: ${{ steps.htp-cache.outputs.cache-hit == 'true' }}
        run: |
          export HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT="$HOME/.hexagon-sdk/$HEXAGON_SDK_VERSION"
          export HEXAGON_TOOLS_ROOT="$HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT/tools/HEXAGON_Tools/$HEXAGON_TOOLS_VERSION"
          npm run build:android

      - name: Save ccache
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/save-ccache

  build-android-libs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      # Runners currently have ~90 GB free, several times what this job needs.
      # Only spend time on cleaning up if that stops being true.
      - name: Free disk space if short
        run: |
          df -h /
          available_gb=$(df --output=avail -BG / | tail -n 1 | tr -dc '0-9')
          if [ "$available_gb" -lt 40 ]; then
            sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc /opt/hostedtoolcache
            df -h /
          fi

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          bootstrap: hexagon-sdk

      # Pin the JDK: with the runner's newer default, a JVM restricted-method
      # warning fails the Android Gradle Plugin's CMake configure.
      - name: Setup JDK 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 17

      - name: Cache Hexagon HTP & OpenCL artifacts
        id: htp-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          path: |
            bin
            vendor/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/v73
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-htp-${{ hashFiles('scripts/build-hexagon-htp.sh', 'scripts/build-opencl.sh', 'scripts/docker-build-wrapper.sh', 'vendor/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/**', 'vendor/OpenCL-Headers/**', 'vendor/OpenCL-ICD-Loader/**') }}

      - name: Setup ccache
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-ccache
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          key: android-libs-${{ hashFiles('vendor/VERSIONS') }}

      # Same steps as `npm run build:android-libs`, except that the DSP libraries
      # and the OpenCL stub are taken from the cache while their sources (the
      # cache key) are unchanged.
      - name: Build libraries
        run: |
          if [ "${{ steps.htp-cache.outputs.cache-hit }}" != "true" ]; then
            ./scripts/build-hexagon-htp.sh
            ./scripts/build-opencl.sh
          fi
          ./scripts/build-android.sh

      # This step exists to prove the prebuilt path works, using the libraries the
      # previous step just built. It has to be -P, not a sed on
      # example/android/gradle.properties: android/gradle.properties force-enables
      # from-source builds for llama.rn, and a subproject's own gradle.properties
      # outranks the root project's. Only the command line beats both.
      - name: Build example for Android
        run: |
          cd example/android
          ./gradlew assembleDebug --stacktrace -PrnllamaBuildFromSource=false

      - name: Save ccache
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/save-ccache
",
  "rationale": "Added explicit job timeouts (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT) to all seven jobs in the workflow. The workflow previously had no timeout bounds, relying on GitHub's 6-hour default. Evidence from experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 shows a 26.8% elapsed-time reduction for a similar lint/typecheck job when a 5-minute timeout was added. Timeouts were set with operational headroom: 10 min for lint (npm lint + typecheck), 20 min for test (JS + C++ unit tests), 30 min for the matrix slice job, and 45 min for the heavier iOS/Android build jobs. This preserves all build/test coverage and required checks while preventing runaway executions. The concurrency cancel-in-progress setting (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) was already present.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
message.reasoning:
Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence to determine if there's a suitable CI optimization to apply.

First, let me understand the current workflow:
- It's a CI workflow with multiple jobs: lint, test, build-ios-from-source, build-ios-frameworks, build-ios-framework-slices, build-android-from-source, build-android-libs
- It uses npm, CocoaPods, Gradle, and various caching mechanisms (ccache, actions/cache)
- The workflow already has some caching in place (ccache, Pods cache, Hexagon HTP cache)

Now let me look at the evidence patterns:

1. **P-LIT-GHA-CACHE** - Cache dependency downloads (multiple examples showing caching Go modules, Gradle dependencies, pip dependencies)
2. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** - Bound jobs with custom timeout (example shows adding timeout-minutes: 5)
3. **P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE** - Share cached build dependencies
4. **P-LIT-ENV-CACHE** - Reuse validated build environments
5. **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** - Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure
6. **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** - Cancel superseded runs (already has concurrency with cancel-in-progress: true)
7. **P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER** - Filter workflow triggers by changed paths
8. **P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW** - Skip explicitly dispensable workflow runs
9. **P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE** - Pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows
10. **P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE** - Suppress schedules during repository inactivity
11. **P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST** - Run previously failing jobs first
12. **P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT** - Derive timeout candidates from successful history
13. **P-LIT-PRIORITIZE** - Prioritize tests for early failure feedback
14. **P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY** - Prioritize queued builds
15. **P-LIT-SELECT** - Select tests using change dependencies
16. **P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT** - Select builds using change or outcome predictions
17. **P-LIT-BAZEL-PARALLEL** - Tune Bazel build parallelism (not applicable, no Bazel)
18. **P-LIT-BAZEL-INCREMENTAL** - Cache Bazel build results (not applicable)
19. **P-LIT-BAZEL-DEPS** - Evaluate dependency cache overhead (not applicable)
20. **P-LIT-UNAFFECTED-STEPS** - Skip steps using traced dependencies
21. **P-LIT-SMELL-REPAIR** - Repair evidenced configuration smells
22. **P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION** - Predict duration to guide investigation
23. **P-LIT-UNUSED-OUTPUTS** - Remove genuinely unused outputs
24. **P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE** - Reuse work across compatible configurations
25. **P-LIT-UNUSED-DEP-SKIP** - Evaluate skipping unused-dependency updates

Looking at the workflow, I can see several jobs that could benefit from optimizations:

1. **Custom timeouts** - The workflow has no explicit timeouts. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to jobs. This could prevent runaway jobs.

2. **Dependency caching** - The workflow already uses some caching (ccache, Pods, Hexagon), but there might be opportunities for more caching. However, the workflow already has extensive caching.

3. **Fail-fast for matrix jobs** - The `build-ios-framework-slices` job uses a matrix strategy but doesn't have `fail-fast: true` (it has `fail-fast: false`). The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST pattern suggests canceling remaining matrix jobs after failure.

4. **Change filtering** - The workflow runs on all pushes/PRs to main. Could potentially filter by changed paths.

Let me check the evidence more carefully:

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) shows a 26.8% elapsed savings by adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job. This is a measured improvement on a fork.

The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST pattern has estimated benefits (2% free, 1.5% paid VM time reduction).

The workflow already has `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, which implements P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE.

Looking at the jobs:
- `lint` - runs npm lint and typecheck
- `test` - runs npm test and C++ tests
- `build-ios-from-source` - builds iOS from source
- `build-ios-frameworks` - builds iOS frameworks
- `build-ios-framework-slices` - matrix job building framework slices
- `build-android-from-source` - builds Android from source
- `build-android-libs` - builds Android libraries

The `build-ios-framework-slices` job has `fail-fast: false` explicitly set. According to P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, we could consider changing this to `fail-fast: true` to cancel remaining matrix jobs after a failure. However, the contraindications include "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required". Since this builds different architecture slices for iOS frameworks, and the comment says "All slices are packaged together by the release and sync workflows", it seems like all slices might be required. But if one fails, the others might not be needed for feedback.

Actually, looking more carefully at the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT evidence, it shows a concrete measured improvement of 26.8% elapsed savings. The pattern has preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists". The workflow has historical runs (shown in ci_history), so this precondition might be met.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern suggests adding explicit timeouts to jobs. Currently, none of the jobs have explicit timeouts. GitHub Actions has a default timeout of 6 hours, but adding shorter timeouts can prevent runaway jobs.

Let me check if there are any jobs that would be good candidates for timeouts. The lint and test jobs are likely fast. The build jobs could take longer. But we need to be careful not to set timeouts too low for valid slow runs.

The evidence shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job that had median elapsed seconds of 41s baseline and 30s optimized. That's a very short job. Our build jobs are likely much longer.

However, the pattern is about "Bound jobs with a custom timeout" and the optimization question is "Assess bound jobs with a custom timeout for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE."

Given that:
1. The workflow has no explicit timeouts
2. There's measured evidence (26.8% savings) for adding timeouts
3. The pattern has preconditions that might be met (historical runs exist)
4. This is a minimal, safe change that preserves all checks

I think adding reasonable timeouts to jobs could be a valid optimization. But I need to choose appropriate timeout values. The evidence shows 5 minutes for a ~40 second job. For our build jobs, we'd need longer timeouts.

Actually, looking at the evidence more carefully, the "Artifact before" and "Artifact after" show a workflow with a single job "checks" that gets `timeout-minutes: 5` added. The job runs lint, typecheck, etc. - similar to our `lint` job.

Our `lint` job runs:
- Checkout
- Setup (custom action)
- npm run lint
- npm run typecheck

This is similar to the evidence example. The `test` job runs more extensive tests.

I could add timeouts to the lint and test jobs, and possibly the build jobs with longer timeouts.

But wait - the instruction says "Preserve the intended build and test coverage, and avoid unrelated changes." Adding timeouts doesn't change coverage, it just bounds execution time.

Also: "Do not weaken permissions or add privileged actions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations or new network access." Timeouts don't do any of these.

Let me also consider P-LIT-FAIL-FAST for the matrix job. The `build-ios-framework-slices` job has `fail-fast: false`. Changing to `fail-fast: true` would cancel remaining matrix jobs on first failure. The contraindications are "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required". The comment says "Every xcframework slice compiles the whole library, so the slices are split over parallel jobs... All slices are packaged together by the release and sync workflows." This suggests all slices are needed for the final package, but for CI feedback, failing fast might be acceptable. However, since the contraindication says "Every matrix outcome is required", and the comment implies all slices are needed, this might not be appropriate.

Given the evidence, I think the strongest candidate is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT with the measured 26.8% savings. The evidence ID is `experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508`.

I'll propose adding reasonable timeouts to the jobs. For the lint job (similar to the evidence example), 5-10 minutes. For test job, maybe 15-20 minutes. For build jobs, longer (30-60 minutes). But I need to be careful not to set them too low.

Actually, looking at the evidence again, the pattern is "P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT" and the example adds `timeout-minutes: 5` at the job level. The workflow in the evidence has a single job. Our workflow has multiple jobs. I should add timeouts to each job.

Let me create an updated workflow with timeouts added to each job. I'll use reasonable values based on typical CI times:
- lint: 10 minutes (npm lint + typecheck)
- test: 20 minutes (npm test + C++ tests)
- build-ios-from-source: 45 minutes
- build-ios-frameworks: 45 minutes
- build-ios-framework-slices: 30 minutes per matrix job
- build-android-from-source: 45 minutes
- build-android-libs: 45 minutes

These are conservative estimates to avoid false timeouts.

Wait, I should check if there's any evidence for what timeout values to use. The P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT pattern is about deriving timeouts from history, but that's a different pattern. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT just says "Choose an explicit budget with operational headroom".

Given the measured evidence shows 26.8% savings for a similar job type (lint/typecheck), and the workflow has no timeouts currently, I think this is a supported optimization.

Let me prepare the updated workflow YAML.
